ink.$description: Ink — Pure black — the structural anchor, used for hairlines, border strokes, and the deepest surface layer beneath imagery

graphite.$description: Graphite — Primary text and dominant UI foreground — body copy, headings, and the off-black tone that softens pure black for large runs of type

paper.$description: Paper — Primary page canvas and white card surfaces.

mist.$description: Mist — Subtle surface wash for cards and elevated panels — the gentlest step off Paper, used where a panel needs to register without shouting

ash.$description: Ash — Tertiary surface and muted background fills — visible only as quiet backing for inactive states or low-emphasis blocks

steel.$description: Steel — Secondary text and subtle UI borders — metadata, timestamps, supporting copy, the mid-gray that bridges Graphite and Ash

pewter.$description: Pewter — Tertiary text and the quietest dividers — labels, tag text, anywhere type needs to recede into the surface

graphik-medium.$description: Primary typeface for all body, headings, and links. The custom Graphik brings humanist warmth that prevents the monochrome palette from feeling cold — paired with aggressive negative tracking (-0.05em at 60px) it compresses headlines into a single film-credit-like line. Weights stay at 400 and 500 only; no bold jumps, only tonal shifts between regular and medium.

lcddot-tr.$description: Rare digital accent — a pixel/dot-matrix display face used for at most one or two elements per page (counters, timestamps, glitch labels). Its positive tracking (+0.025em to +0.04em) and rigid grid construction create a single moment of machine voice in an otherwise humanist system, like a digital readout appearing in a dark room.

system-sans-serif.$description: Fallback micro-text — utility copy, browser-rendered labels, or fallback rendering when custom fonts fail to load
